This review therefore built two scratch trees from the reviewed commit's own object store -- git archive of 509f1236 and of the reviewed head 59a51cb1 into $TMPDIR/arms/base and $TMPDIR/arms/head under this node's node-local scratch; no git worktree created and neither the reviewed object store nor its worktree written -- and ran the reviewed node's declared retention gate in each. findings.text: The reviewed run did not produce the evidence fragment its own FENCE-SCOPE names and the CONTRACT-LANDING YOUR RECORD requires ('The fragment goes into your final commit'). Its single commit 59a51cb1 touches only imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_retention.py and tests/test_telemetry_retention.py; the fragment path does not exist on disk and no commit adds it. The run's stream shows the worker deliberated and chose no fragment on the reading that its done-when names no artifact (prompt line 56, 'this node writes no evidence fragment'), but that clause exempts prose and figures *inside* the fragment, not the fragment itself, and every sibling section-8 node reviewed so far commits one (the immediately preceding reviewed run's commit e7fa17da added a 97-line fragment). This is a delivery-anchor gap rather than a code defect: promotion lands the manifest's landing line on the plan section, so the node is promotable, but the plan's evidence page gains no durable anchor for this node. The worker's own stream names it 'the one thing this run did not produce'.

item_verdicts.goal: The node's goal -- treat a file as a raw serving receipt only when its first parseable row carries the job id its name claims -- is met exactly. is_raw_receipt (telemetry_retention.py:263) now requires receipts_job_id(path) not None, then reads the first parseable JSON object via the new private _first_row (line 237) and returns str(row.get('job_id')) == job. The false-candidacy mechanism the goal targets is real and was confirmed at the name level: _JOB_ID_IN_NAME is `-(\d+)\.jsonl(?:\.\d+)?(?:\.gz)?\Z` (telemetry_index.py:176), so `requests-2026-10-01.jsonl` matches on its `-01.jsonl` tail with group '01' -- a name-only test admits it. The module docstring's opening list now states the row check as the FIRST qualifying condition and the old false claim ('a request receipt carries no job id at all') is gone from the is_raw_receipt docstring and replaced by an accurate sentence naming exactly why the rotation is refused.
